Final Grade Checker

Manual entry or paste from your grade export. Grades calculate automatically.

Everything stays in this browser tab. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is saved, unless you explicitly check "Remember these settings" in Grading Settings below — which only ever remembers the rounding/weighting settings, never a student's name or grades.

Grading Settings

These change how every grade on this page is calculated — including exports and slips. They apply only in this tab for this session unless you check "Remember" at the bottom. The defaults below match the Carroll County rule described under the grade cards.

Paste rows directly from your grade system. Each row should have a student ID, name, section, grade level, and four quarter grades like C(73.28). The system average column at the end is ignored. Paste with tabs between columns so an empty quarter stays in its own column — or drop a .csv/.xlsx export onto this box, or choose one below.

Import warnings
    Column mapping

    If a gradebook export changed column order and the importer guessed wrong, set the columns explicitly here from the first row below, then re-import.

    Which grade to use? Per Carroll County grading policy, award the higher of the two methods. The highlighted box is the one to report.
    Quality Points: Each quarter letter converts to a point value (A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0). Those four values are averaged, then converted back to a letter (3.5 and up is an A).
    Percentage Average: The four raw percentages are averaged directly, then converted using the 10-point scale. Exactly .5 rounds up, so 89.5 is an A and 89.49 is a B.
    All four quarters are required. With a quarter missing or exempt, no final grade is shown, because a three-quarter average is not the county's number.
    A (90–100)
    B (80–89)
    C (70–79)
    D (60–69)
    F (below 60)

    What Do I Need on the Remaining Quarter?

    Enter the quarters you already know, mark which one is still open, and set a target final grade. This solves the same two county rules used above — Quality Points and Percentage Average — for the score needed on the open quarter, using whichever method gets there with the lower score. Each quarter counts equally: 25% of the final grade.
